metadata.case_name: CHAN KUN v. TSUEN WAN NEW CAMBRIDGE NURSING HOME LTD AND OTHERS

source: She was found to have sustained right femur fracture with the bone being osteoporotic, as well as sores over her back, right elbow and right foot.

injuries.description: malunion after previous fracture of right elbow (deformed and ankyosed right elbow)
source: X-rays of her deformed and ankyosed right elbow reveal malunion after previous fracture.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the elbow or forearm

injuries.description: fracture of right upper tibia (occurred while under rehabilitation at CMC in May)
source: The part played by the advanced degree of osteoporosis of her bones as the cause of the fracture is further supported by the fracture of her right upper tibia while she was under rehabilitation at CMC in May this year.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of upper end of tibia

injuries.description: bedsores / pressure sores over limbs (including left toe and heel and sores over back, right elbow and right foot)
injuries.body_part: limbs / back / right elbow / right foot / left toe and heel
source: Because of her prolonged stay in bed and the contracture of her limbs giving rise to pressure points, the Plaintiff had bedsores over her limbs.
On 13th June 2002, the Plaintiff was admitted to the Department of Orthopaedics & Traumatology of Yan Chai Hospital for cellulitis of her left leg and bedsores over the left toe and heel.

injuries.description: three episodes of cerebrovascular accident (1993, 1998 and 1999) resulting in paralysis/being bedridden and inability to speak
source: According to the joint medical report, the Plaintiff had three episodes of cerebrovascular accident in 1993, 1998 and 1999.
The Plaintiff is paraplegic and unable to speak.
Concerning the likely cause of the fracture of her right femur, both Dr. Lau and Dr. Tsoi agree that the main cause should be the extremely osteoporotic bones subsequent to the prolonged stay in bed.
She had contracture of her 4 limbs in spite of maintenance exercises.

manifestations.description: dependent on others for her personal care including cleansing, bathing, putting on clothes and feeding
could no longer walk but was staying in bed most of the time though she could sit up in the bed or in the wheelchair at times
poor response to external stimuli such as words spoken by her son and relatives
right leg was dangling, and that her facial expression showed that she was having severe pain
PW1 noticed that the Plaintiff’s right knee was pointing effortless away from her body, and that her right thigh was red and denting inward like a "V"
eyes were wide open, her face was red and she was making some noises
stomach tube feeding (fed via stomach tube between 29th June 2002 and 19th July 2002 and on 26th July 2002 fed at 6 a.m., 10 a.m. and 2 p.m. with 250 ml. of milk and 50 ml. of water on each occasion)
contracture of limbs (limbs held tightly together)

treatments_received: admitted into the Princess Margaret Hospital and completed a program of rehabilitation and physiotherapy
discharged to the Nursing Home on 12th November 1999
admitted to the Department of Orthopaedics & Traumatology of Yan Chai Hospital on 26th July 2002 and treated conservatively for the fracture
stayed in Yan Chai Hospital until March 2003 when she was transferred to Caritas Medical Centre due to the outbreak of atypical pneumonia
transferred in June 2003 to Kowloon Hospital and is now staying in the rehabilitation unit of the Hospital
stomach tube feeding (fed via stomach tube between 29th June 2002 and 19th July 2002)

losses.description: Pain and suffering from the fracture to her right femur and subsequent mal-union; judge described outcome as "pain and suffering rather than loss of amenities of life" and awarded PSLA.
